prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
competitors_mentioned: Rich Results Test and Search Console
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “ChatGPT directory” — the best way is to make sure your business appears in the major knowledge sources (Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps, industry directories) and then (1) claim/manage those listings and (2) test appearance in AI assistants. For auditing and ongoing monitoring, BrightLocal or Yext are the most useful services.

Why, and what to do
- ChatGPT and similar LLM-based assistants don’t consult one public directory. Their recommendations come from a mix of: their training data, real-time web search / plugins (if enabled), and knowledge graphs built by Google, Microsoft, Yelp, etc. So being “recommended” depends on being present/authoritative in those underlying sources.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (most important), Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps, and any vertical directories (TripAdvisor, Zocdoc, etc.). Use consistent NAP (name, address, phone).
  2. Add LocalBusiness schema.org structured data to your website and verify it with Google’s Rich Results Test and Search Console.
  3. Collect and respond to reviews (Google & Yelp matter a lot).
  4. Build citations on reputable local directories and get a few authoritative backlinks.

Best services to check/monitor
- BrightLocal — local search audits, citation checks, rank tracking in local pack across search engines; good for testing how you appear to search-based assistants.
- Yext — centralized listings management and distribution to many directories; useful if you want to push updates to multiple knowledge providers and see where you appear.
- Moz Local / Whitespark — good citation monitoring and local rank tracking (Whitespark is strong for local citations).
- Google Search Console + Google Business Profile dashboard — to see how Google shows your business (search queries, impressions, knowledge panel).
- Reputation tools (ReviewTrackers, Birdeye) — monitor reviews which heavily influence recommendations.

How to test actual AI recommendations
- Direct testing: Ask the assistants themselves, e.g. in ChatGPT (with browsing/plugins enabled), Bard, and Bing Chat. Use location-aware prompts like “I’m in [city, ZIP]. Recommend a reputable [service] within 5 miles with 4+ star reviews.” Try multiple phrasings and incognito/cleared cookies to reduce personalization bias.
- Automated / scaled: Use BrightLocal’s Local Rank Tracker and similar tools to simulate queries and see if you appear in local packs and featured snippets (which search-based assistants pull from).

Short checklist
- Claim Google Business Profile + Bing Places + Yelp
- Add LocalBusiness schema to site and test it
- Ensure NAP consistency across directories
- Gather reviews (Google & Yelp especially)
- Use BrightLocal (audit + rank tracking) and Yext (distribution) for ongoing monitoring

If you tell me your business type and city, I can recommend the single most important listing(s) to claim first and give a sample prompt to test in ChatGPT/Bing/Bard.
